newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania won't cut tariffs despite IMF suggestion.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania won't cut tariffs despite IMF suggestion.

text.p: Lithuania said on Wednesday that it would refuse to cut further its import tariffs despite International Monetary Fund (IMF) recommendations that the rates be reduced to liberalise trade.
"We will keep to our position very strongly...we think that a stop must be given to tariff reductions," Economy Minister Vincas Babilius told Reuters after meeting an IMF mission.
The mission is in Lithuania to review how the Baltic state is performing under the terms of its credits from the Fund.
Lithuania said it should not cut tariffs further than has been agreed with trading partners.
"The dispute is mainly over a basket of eight agricultural products...we have already cut these tariffs to 27.7 percent from 44 percent, and this is our limit," Babilius.
He said the IMF wanted the tariffs cut to 20 percent.
Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius has said thr import tariffs could not be reduced any more because domestic producers were already facing too much competition.
The government also said it was discussing changes to monetary policy.
Lithuania wants to scrap its currency board system of keeping the litas pegged to the dollar and replacing it with a peg maintained through central bank open-market operations.
